text: Welcome to week three of the official
NASCAR Gen4 Cup Series. This week you'll
be heading to the New Hampshire Motor
Speedway for 80 laps.
Assuming iRacing has the right
conditions set on the schedule, the
track's going to be slick this week. So,
once you get into qualifying, make sure
you warm your tires and prime your
brakes.
Run your warm-up and first laps at speed
while avoiding tire scrub, and be sure
to give yourself as much room as
possible in turns three and four to
build momentum for your final time to
lap.
As you hit turn one, get on the brakes
and aim the car at the lowest banked
portion of the track. The car will slide
up naturally through the center, and you
can use that to your advantage.
Roll up the track as you slow the car
down for the center of the corner, and
gently get back on the throttle as you
turn the car down the track.
Make your way down the back stretch and
hit turn three with a similar approach.
Brake, turn in, arc up the track in the
center, and ease back onto the throttle
as you point your nose out of the
corner.
Try not to spin your rear tires as you
accelerate to the finish line.
Let's see that lap again.
Let's crank it up.
Once the race begins, they'll be
starting gingerly in second gear. Your
initial approach will depend on which
lane you start in.
If you're on the inside, you'll want to
run a shallow line around the lowest
banked portion of the track. And if
you're on the outside, you'll want to
run a lane higher and give yourself as
much momentum as you can as you hit the
backstretch.
Once the field begins to spread out,
your next priority should be to run the
lower lane and save your right side
tires. While the outside line proved
quicker from the start of the run, in
just 15 laps there was a clear
difference in the right side tire wear,
favoring the lower line.
With that in mind, if you find yourself
deep in the field, you'll be better off
running conservatively around the second
and third lanes. The biggest weakness of
the inside line is that if you don't
have access to the full width of the
track, you will be forced to square off
your exits, and that will quickly
degrade your right side tires.
The car trends loose over the course of
the run regardless of which line you
take, but the drivers who will see the
most success this week will be the ones
who take it easy from the beginning.
Starting up front will be an easy way to
see that through, as getting the whole
shot into turn one will almost guarantee
open pavement by the end of turn two.
Another factor to consider will be your
tire strategy.
As you may have noticed on both tire
readings, the left sides don't see
nearly as much wear as the handling
would suggest. Now, I'm not saying that
taking two tires on a late race caution
would be an easy choice, but considering
the number of cautions I've seen at this
track, you may be able to pull it off
under the right circumstances, but be
careful.
Tire spin is guaranteed on almost every
single restart here, so mismatching your
tires may offer results outside of your
expectations.
As is tradition when the official series
visit New Hampshire, there will also be
a lot of people over driving their cars.
Whether they're chucking themselves down
onto the flat on entry, spinning their
tires on exit, or just completely
misjudging their reference points.
You'll need to keep eyes on every corner
of your car when the field's stacked up.
If you can do that, manage your tires,
and make the right calls on the box, you
could find yourself holding the winning
lobster in victory lane.
Good luck.
